standard_prerequisites.name: Inconsistency in natural deduction
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set Gamma is inconsistent when falsity is derivable from undischarged assumptions in Gamma.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the assumption the contrapositive starts from (2392-2395).

standard_prerequisites.name: Soundness of natural deduction
standard_prerequisites.statement: Everything derivable from Gamma is entailed by Gamma; the unit proves this as its soundness theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: It forces every satisfying structure to satisfy the derived falsity (2395-2398).

core_obligations: Contrapositive setup: assume Gamma is inconsistent, so falsity has a derivation from undischarged assumptions in Gamma (2392-2395).
By soundness, every structure satisfying Gamma satisfies falsity (2395-2398).
No structure satisfies falsity, so no structure satisfies Gamma; Gamma is unsatisfiable, proving the contrapositive (2398-2401).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack inconsistency as a derivation of falsity.
Apply soundness and rule out satisfiability.

difficulty_reason: The counted corollary is the author corollary at source lines 2385-2388: a satisfiable set of sentences is consistent in the natural deduction calculus. The author proof (2390-2401) runs the contrapositive: an inconsistency is a derivation of falsity from Gamma, soundness forces every satisfying structure to satisfy falsity, which no structure can, so Gamma is unsatisfiable. The identification of inconsistency with derivability of the false constant and the appeal to the unit's soundness theorem are the counted moves.
